summary.whatChanges: Rewrites the IPv4-in-IPv6 branch of `expandIPv6` to compute the two trailing hex groups directly from the dotted-quad octets instead of round-tripping through the binary conversion helpers. Fixes expansion of addresses whose embedded IPv4 part yields zero groups, and adds test cases covering them.
behaviorChanges: expandIPv6('::ffff:0.0.0.1') now returns the fully expanded '0000:...:ffff:0000:0001' instead of a malformed/compressed result
expandIPv6('::0.0.0.0') expands to eight zero groups
Embedded IPv4 suffixes in full-length addresses (e.g. '2001:db8:1:2:3:4:0.0.0.1') expand correctly
Anything comparing or matching expanded IPv6 strings (e.g. IP-based restriction) now matches these previously mis-expanded addresses
risks: Octets are parsed with Number without range/count validation; malformed input passing the regex could yield NaN or wrong hex groups
Bitwise `<<` coerces to 32-bit signed ints; out-of-range octet values would silently wrap instead of erroring
Output hex groups are unpadded here and rely on the subsequent padding loop; any change to that loop would break results
